title: Coordinated distribution & release-notes playbook for staged model catalog additions
creator: Priya Nair
description: Purpose: Provide a prescriptive, cross-team playbook for shipping new model entries into the public Redwood model catalog. This ticket centralizes the tasks required to (1) validate model performance and safety gates, (2) coordinate release notes and marketing assets, (3) publish catalog metadata and SDK mappings, and (4) run a staged rollout with clear rollback criteria. Scope: new open models and model-variants that will be visible in the hosted API and surfaced in the Console model catalog. Out of scope: enterprise-only private deployments (handled via Dedicated/Private playbooks).
checklist: Create canonical catalog entry (model name, version, tags, license, supported APIs)
Attach benchmark summary: latency P50/P95, throughput, memory footprint (quant & fp), and cost-per-token estimate
Upload benchmark artifacts: perf scripts, raw results, seed prompts, and scoring harness link
Run qualitative evals on Redwood golden prompt set and record failures/patterns
Safety review: checklist passed and any mitigations documented
Docs tasks: update model card, API examples, SDK mapping, and migration notes
Release notes draft: one-line summary, key metrics, known limitations, recommended use cases
Internal announcement draft: TL;DR, changelog entry, support Q&A, priority customers to notify
External announcement plan: blog outline, release highlights, benchmark callouts, timeline
Console changes: add model tile, default config presets, and recommended routing policy
SDK updates: default model alias + compatibility note in SDK changelog
E2E smoke tests: generation/sample prompts, embeddings sanity checks, and function-call flow
Canary rollout plan: gradated traffic percentages and time windows
Monitoring & SLOs: dashboards and alerts created for perf regressions and error spikes
Rollback plan: automatic fallback to previous model variant and manual roll-back runbook
Support enablement: create internal FAQ, troubleshooting runbook, and training session
Legal/License sign-off: confirm redistribution/derivatives constraints documented
Marketing assets: blog draft, social copy, benchmark visualizations, and customer emails
Partners & marketplace: notify channel partners and update marketplace listing if applicable
Post-launch postmortem template scheduled for 2 weeks after full rollout

acceptance_criteria: Catalog entry is live in staging and visible via API with complete metadata
Benchmark summary published with reproducible artifacts
Release notes published to /releases and linked from model card
Console tile updated and visible to beta orgs
Canary rollout executed with no severity incidents for 48h
Support team has internal FAQ and passed a live walkthrough
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): internal orgs only, validate end-to-end integrations (48 hours)
Phase 1 (canary): 10% traffic for 24 hours, monitor latency/error-rate/SLOs
Phase 2 (ramp): 30% traffic for 48 hours if no regressions, verify cost metrics
Phase 3 (full): 100% traffic and public announcement; keep heightened monitoring for 72 hours
Auto-fallback: On P95 > baseline +30% or error-rate spike >3x baseline for 10m, route to previous model variant
Manual rollback: PM + Eng lead approval required; full rollback runbook in links
post_launch_monitoring: Alert: latency-p95-breach (> baseline +20%) — P1 on-call escalation
Alert: error-rate-spike (>3x baseline) — immediate rollback recommendation
Usage anomaly detection: sudden change in distribution of sequence lengths or token types
Support ticket queue filter: tag new model-related tickets with 'pm-9933'
notes: Trade-offs: we prioritized shipping a well-documented model card and reproducible benchmarks over an aggressive marketing timeline. If ENG-3520 patch introduces a notable perf improvement, we'll delay external announcement by up to one week to include updated numbers. Keep comms conservative: highlight recommended use-cases and list known limitations clearly to reduce support load.
